digest.component_or_area: Jira integration adapters (Cloud vs. Data Center backends)
propositions: Jira Cloud and Data Center differ on three axes: REST protocol version (v3 vs. v2), text encoding (ADF vs. wiki-markup), and user identity (accountId vs. name), requiring a unified adapter architecture that does not fork logic.

The existing value maps for status/priority transitions exist in three independent copies that have already drifted (deleted key present in two copies but missing in the third), creating a single-sourcing problem.

Location-pinned modules (adf.py, outbound_fields.py, comment_limits.py) are loaded by file path via dynamic loader and cannot relocate; instead of moving them, the epic achieves single-sourcing through dependency inversion by having pinned modules import and use jira_family contracts.

The Jira Data Center backend requires TLS verification by default (rejecting non-https URLs unless explicitly overridden), reads the PAT only from environment variables (never from config files), and discovers resolved workflow states from operator configuration rather than assuming Cloud's hardcoded names.

Two implementations of one contract per axis of variation (RichTextCodec: AdfCodec for Cloud, WikiTextCodec for DC; UserIdentityModel: AccountIdIdentity for Cloud, NameIdentity for DC) is the correct design, not a violation of single-sourcing.

The live Jira Data Center oracle (Dockerized 8.17.1 instance at localhost:2990) is locally built not pulled, demonstrates bidirectional reconciliation of real issues through both inbound and outbound passes with zero unhandled exceptions, and proves data round-trips correctly.
